text:
release-manager: Heads-up — prod canary for payment-service v3.4.1 failed to promote. Deploybot halted during the 18:00 change window. Need quick call: pin to v3.4.0 digest or force hotfix rollover? :warning:

deploybot: ERROR deploy blocked: IMAGE_PIN_MISMATCH across registries. root manifest digest in release-manifest: sha256:aa11bb22cc33, observed published digest in eu-west-1: sha256:dd44ee55ff66. Code: ERR_IMAGE_PIN_MISMATCH

ci-bot: Pushed build artifacts at 1715007600. multi-arch manifest created. All checks passed in CI, but registry mirror may have served older manifest during replicate window.

ana (ana): @release-manager @jason I can take the pin if we decide — can push a manual pin or re-run publish. Which option preserves DB-migration safety? :eyes:

jason: Context — v3.4.1 includes the DB migration that increases per-worker memory footprint (low risk but noticed in canary). Ops suggested hold if memory regressions continue. We should avoid forcing it until we confirm runtime mem profile.

release-manager: Right. Canary showed one pod OOM 3m after startup in eu-west-1 canary (not in us-central). That aligns with the manifest mismatch — not sure which artifact ran. We need a deterministic rollback path for release notes and the migration.

matt-oncall: If we pin to v3.4.0 digest we eliminate migration risk immediately. Rollback steps are simple: kubectl set image or update deploy manifest to pinned digest and redeploy via deploybot. ETA ~10m for me to coordinate. :+1:

deploybot: To pin manually, run:
```
# update k8s deployment image to pinned digest
kubectl set image deploy/payment-service payment-service=123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/payment-service@sha256:aa11bb22cc33 --namespace=prod
# then trigger deploybot promotion: /deploy promote payment-service --from-manual
```
Note: deploybot will reject pushes if the release-manifest digest != registry digest.

lily: From product — we prefer pin + delay migration. Please add a short release note: "Held migration for payment-service; will re-run after memory regression investigation." I can draft.

sasha: Ops note — eu-west replication sometimes lags ~30-90s. The observed dd44... digest looks like a stale mirror or orphaned manifest. We should avoid forcing republish until we confirm KMS annotations and attestation match. Trying a re-sync would be noisy during the window.

ana (ana): Given the risk, I'm for pinning. I can pin and update rollout strategy to a conservative canary (1->5) and leave a canary flag.

jason: Agreed. Decision: pin to sha256:aa11bb22cc33 (v3.4.0) for now, hold v3.4.1 promotion. Resolve registry mirror/digest drift after hours, retest migration on staging, then re-schedule migration in next change window.

release-manager: Action items: @ana pin and promote (matt oncall to watch), @lily add release-note blurb, @sasha file a registry replication incident with digest details (include logs), @jason follow up on migration test plan. I'll update the public release notes and close the change window.

matt-oncall: Pin in progress. Will report back on rollout status in ~8m. :eyes:

deploybot: Promotion succeeded: payment-service pinned to sha256:aa11bb22cc33 and deployment rolled to 3 replicas stable. Promotion event: 1715007815.

matt-oncall: Rollout verified in eu-west-1 — no OOMs observed after 10m. Holding release.

lily: Drafted release-note: "Rollback: payment-service migration held due to registry digest mismatch and observed canary memory spike. Teams investigating; new rollout will be scheduled after validation." Posting to release notes doc. :memo:

sasha: Created incident ticket REG-3421 with digest diffs and mirror timestamps, assigned to infra-team.

release-manager: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after infra completes the sync investigation. Closing thread for the window. :lock:
